verification.summary: The provider-free smoke ran green twice consecutively with one worker and zero retries on the closed bytes, plus a post-commit confirmation run, after env-setup proved provider-free readiness for the native store. The single test establishes a run-stable virtual product idempotently over REST, asserts the gateway-enabled precondition, gates on the payment element genuinely mounting with an accessibly named frame and all three card fields, then performs three invalid-input gestures once each from asserted valid baselines: a Luhn-failing card number, a past expiration date, and an incomplete security code. Each rejection must mark its exact field invalid and reference a non-empty alert error element through the field description, polled as one predicate; each correction must restore a value-verified valid field with the description withdrawn and focus resting where the shopper left it. The run proves zero Store API checkout dispatches across both route forms and an unchanged product-scoped order count. The oracle was mutation-checked in three directions on the closed bytes: renaming the payment-element container in the built integration fails the mount gate while the REST precondition stays green, feeding a valid card number where the invalid one belongs fails exactly at the invalid-state assertion, and disabling the gateway kills the run loudly at admin authentication before any assertion.

The full controller passed on the closed proposal before commit: the contract-map validator unit tests, the ledger validation across all 181 contracts including the six reopened rows, the project-routing validator unit tests including the six new annotation bindings, the environment-setup contract tests, and the provider-free harness unit tests.

reviews.summary: Two-round review; the first round blocked on evidence attributability because the working tree had moved past the reviewed commit, and every substantive finding was applied before the final bytes were committed and re-verified. On the committed bytes: each gesture opens with an asserted valid baseline on its own field, so the rejection it asserts is provably caused by its own input; recovery asserts the corrected value before the invalid flag and then polls that no non-empty alert description lingers, closing the remounted-empty-field masquerade; the frame is derived from the gated element so gate and interaction target are the same iframe by construction; and a header comment records the owner-accepted downscope for the mounts the smoke does not visit. The product-scoped order filter was verified honoured on both order-storage backends, all six contract annotations resolve one-to-one to ledger rows listing this spec, and the fresh green runs plus both mutation kills describe exactly the shipped bytes.

Two-round review; both findings resolved on the committed bytes. Locators are role-based throughout with no timing waits, and the association proof retries the full invalid-flag, description, alert-element, non-empty-text chain as one atomic polled unit, resolving the non-atomic-read race. Expiry inputs use the suite’s established unformatted four-digit convention. The commit also hardens beyond the requested fixes: proven valid baselines before each gesture, recovery assertions checking corrected value and withdrawn description rather than just the invalid flag, focus verification after each blur, and frame derivation from the exact element the visibility gate proved. The zero-submission and product-scoped order-count oracle held across all gestures.

Two-round review; both findings resolved on the committed bytes. Every REST-backed setup and precondition failure now carries HTTP status and response body, and the association predicate polls as a single unit with a descriptive message, so a split DOM commit can no longer produce a misleading association failure under the zero-retry policy. The gateway precondition and three-field mount gate fail loudly before any accessibility assertion, confirmed under mutation; no exception swallowing, no cross-gesture state leakage, and the additional causal-attribution hardening from other reviewers introduces no new reliability gap.

Two-round review; all four findings resolved on the committed bytes. Association and announcement are established by a single polled predicate that resolves every identifier in the field’s description list and requires one to be a non-empty alert element — genuinely state-sensitive, since the description list is identical in valid and invalid states and only the resolved node differs. Recovery proves the alert description is withdrawn, so a latched message a screen-reader user would still hear on a corrected field now fails, and a corrected-value assertion prevents a remount masquerading as recovery. Focus is asserted on the clicked field after each blur, witnessing that the error does not steal the shopper’s place in the form. The closure claims programmatic exposure and field association under the relevant success criteria, not verified assistive-technology utterance, and records the provider-owned traits — the alert node injected with its text, the polite live-region override, and inter-subfield auto-advance — as inherited, not introduced.

Two-round review; approved and re-confirmed on independently hashed committed bytes. The test card data is the provider’s published public test numbers with a flipped check digit, safe to commit; no assertion captures request bodies or provider telemetry, so nothing sensitive reaches traces or artifacts; all REST calls go through the capability-checked admin fixture with compile-time literals in query strings; no capability check or validation is bypassed; and the zero-dispatch counter plus product-scoped order equality genuinely bound the run’s effect surface. The hardening round added only stronger assertions with no new sink, capture surface, or call.

Obtained per the packets’ named roles and re-confirmed on the committed bytes. Both runtimes mount the same provider payment element in deferred-intent mode with equivalent validation-relevant options, so field-level validation and its accessibility exposure are provider-owned and identical across runtimes. Five introduced divergences were found and recorded, none constrained by the six contracts under closure: a deliberate container and selector rename that merchant styling targeting the old classes will miss, the absence of the client’s loading skeleton, a payment-method option accessible name derived from the visible label where the client hardcodes a product name, a locale-derivation difference that can change the language of in-element validation messages for region-variant locales, and a submit-path difference in how failed payment-method-creation attempts are recorded. The locale and submit-path items are recommended parity follow-ups outside this closure.

Obtained per the My Account packet’s named role and re-confirmed on the committed bytes. The oracle is genuinely copy-free: it couples to nothing the provider authors except standard accessibility semantics, after the provider id-naming heuristic was replaced with a convention-free predicate accepting any field-description target that is itself a non-empty alert element, with failure diagnostics that carry no provider text. The downscope cedes only copy meaningfulness, which the provider alone authors and owns, while proving field association and input-driven recovery more rigorously than the exact-string originals did. Provider strings persist only inside the immutable contract-ledger identifiers as provenance, and the English accessible-name locators fail loudly rather than falsely passing on a localized store.
